definition: Derogatory slang for a gay or effeminate man; literally 'chicken,' invoking cowardice and unmanliness.
notes: Less severe than 'viado'; primarily targets effeminacy or perceived cowardice rather than gay identity per se; the ordinary word for chicken creates contextual ambiguity.

definition: Slur for a gay man; literally 'fruit,' a direct semantic parallel to the English gay slur 'fruit' or 'fruitcake.'
notes: Less common than 'viado' or 'baitola'; the parallel to English 'fruit' is exact and likely intentional; slightly dated but still recognized.

definition: Diminutive of 'fruto'; a slightly softer slur for an effeminate or young gay man; literally 'little fruit.'
notes: The diminutive -inha softens the slur and can imply youth or small build; sometimes used mock-affectionately within gay communities; functions as a gentler register of 'fruto.'

definition: Highly offensive Brazilian slur for a gay man, particularly one perceived as passive or effeminate; etymology disputed, possibly northeastern dialectal in origin.
notes: Severity roughly equivalent to 'viado'; strongly associated with northeastern Brazil but understood nationwide; not reclaimed to any meaningful degree.

definition: Highly offensive pejorative for a travesti or transgender woman; derived from 'travesti' with the contemptuous augmentative suffix -eco.
notes: 'Travesti' is the neutral or community-reclaimed term; 'traveco' is unambiguously pejorative. Travestis are a culturally distinct gender category in Brazil, not simply equivalent to Western transgender women; the -eco suffix signals contempt.

definition: A man whose homosexuality is highly visible and unmistakable; from 'pinta' (mark, sign), meaning one who shows obvious signs of being gay.
notes: Emphasizes visibility of gay identity rather than effeminacy per se; 'pintoso' (m.) also used; can be pejorative or community-affirmative depending on speaker; derived from the idiom 'ter pinta de' (to look like, to give off signs of).

definition: In gay community slang, a descriptor for a man — typically a bottom — defined by having a large, prominent buttocks; from 'bunda' (butt) + augmentative -udo.
notes: In straight usage simply means 'large-butted' (neutral or complimentary); in gay community the term carries the additional implication of receptive sexual role; the big butt becomes the identity marker for the bottom role.

definition: Brazilian gay community pejorative for a promiscuous or sexually very available gay bottom; the augmentative -ona implies excess or disparagingly large scale.
notes: Used primarily within gay communities; etymology uncertain — possibly from a root meaning 'hole' or availability; the -ona augmentative intensifies and feminizes, adding a contemptuous valence; not widely known outside LGBTQ+ communities.

definition: Traditionally, a masculine man who has sex with gay or feminized men while assuming the active role and not identifying as gay; more recently reclaimed to mean simply a masculine or handsome gay man.
notes: Reflects the Latin American sexual system in which active/passive role — not partner gender — historically defined gay identity; the 'bofe' was categorically not gay in older usage despite male-male sex. The closest English subculture term is 'trade.' Now somewhat dated as Brazil's sexual identity framework has westernized.

definition: Dated coded euphemism for a gay or LGBTQ+ person; literally 'one who understands,' used as an in-group shibboleth when open gay identity was dangerous or stigmatized.
notes: Functioned as a secret signal in Brazil from roughly the 1950s through the 1980s; 'entendida' applied to lesbians; now almost entirely replaced by 'gay,' 'lésbica,' 'bicha,' etc.; the low crude score reflects its deliberate innocuousness as a coded term. Primarily known by LGBTQ+ people of the older generation and historians of Brazilian gay culture.

definition: Augmentative of 'gay'; a very or flamboyantly gay man; the -zão suffix implies exaggerated, visible, or over-the-top gayness.
notes: Tone is highly context-dependent — affirmative within community, dismissive or mocking from outsiders; the augmentative does not imply critique in all uses; common in humor, social media, and casual conversation.

definition: Diminutive of 'fresco'; a man who is mildly effeminate or slightly gay-seeming; literally 'a little fresh/cool'; softer register of the slur 'fresco.'
notes: The diminutive -inho substantially reduces the offense and is often used teasingly or ironically; implies low-level effeminacy rather than a full accusation of homosexuality; sometimes used quasi-affectionately within male friend groups.

definition: Slur for an effeminate or cowardly man who fails to conform to masculine norms; frequently applied to gay men; derived from the female name Maria.
notes: Shared with European Portuguese; the -icas suffix is an Iberian morpheme unusual in Brazilian Portuguese, giving it a slightly old-fashioned or foreign quality; still widely understood and actively used; emphasizes gender nonconformity over sexual orientation.

definition: Common and widely used slang for an effeminate, prissy, or gay man; literally 'fresh/cool' but pejoratively implies fussiness, effeminacy, or homosexuality.
notes: One of the most widely used Brazilian terms for effeminate men; less severe than 'viado'; 'fazer fresco' (to make fresco) = to be unnecessarily fussy or demanding; used both for actual gay men and for straight men perceived as insufficiently masculine.

definition: Standard adjective meaning effeminate; applied to men whose behavior, appearance, or mannerisms are perceived as feminine; functions as description or slur depending on context and speaker.
notes: The most clinical of the terms in this cluster; used in journalism, medical, and legal discourse without necessarily being pejorative; higher technical score reflects this semi-clinical register; pejorative force is entirely context-dependent.

definition: In Brazilian drag queen and travesti culture, the state of being fully assembled in femme presentation — hair, makeup, costume, and persona all complete; from 'montar' (to assemble, to mount).
notes: A positive insider term; the antonym is 'desmontada' (out of drag, undone). Not a slur; primarily used within drag and travesti communities and adjacent audiences. The 'mounting' metaphor implies constructing or building an alter-persona, distinct from simply wearing women's clothing.

definition: A masculine-presenting woman or butch lesbian; compound of the female name Maria and 'macho' (male), marking the incongruity between gender presentation and expected femininity.
notes: Shared with Spanish; can be pejorative, neutral, or even self-affirming depending on context; less severe than 'sapatão' or equivalent hardcore slurs; widely understood across all age groups and regions of Brazil.

definition: Literally 'female truck driver'; used as a slur or stereotype for a butch or masculine-presenting lesbian, invoking blue-collar masculine occupation as a mark of gender deviance.
notes: The truck driver archetype for butch women is cross-cultural; 'caminhoneiro' carries strong masculine blue-collar associations in Brazil; the feminine grammatical suffix -eira signals the incongruity that generates the stereotype. Can be used humorously within the community.

definition: 'Son of a whore'; the primary all-purpose strong expletive in Brazilian Portuguese, used both as a targeted insult and as a non-directed exclamation of frustration, pain, or surprise.
notes: The single most common severe expletive in Brazilian Portuguese; 'puta' (whore) is the vulgar element; the literal meaning (calling someone the son of a sex worker) is largely semantically bleached in most uses; functions across nearly all emotional registers when intensification is needed.

definition: Feminine form of 'filho da puta'; literally 'daughter of a whore'; directed at women or used gender-neutrally; identical force and function to the masculine form.
notes: Less frequent than the masculine default 'filho da puta' but universally understood; the feminine grammatical marking can carry the additional sting of calling the target herself the offspring of a sex worker; also used as a non-directed exclamation.

definition: Initialism for 'filho da puta'; used in text, social media, journalism, and any context where the full form is too explicit; decoded instantly by virtually all Brazilian adults.
notes: The abbreviation reduces surface vulgarity without diminishing communicative force; common in WhatsApp, Twitter/X, and Brazilian political commentary; bypasses automated profanity filters while remaining fully understood; the periods are often dropped: 'fdp.'

definition: 'Go fuck yourself'; a direct and emphatic dismissal using the formal subjunctive imperative 'vá' (go) + reflexive 'se foder' (to fuck oneself).
notes: The formal subjunctive 'vá' (rather than colloquial 'vai') adds rhetorical weight; 'foder' is the standard vulgar verb for sexual intercourse; one of the harshest dismissal insults in Brazilian Portuguese; the colloquial variant 'vai se foder' / 'vai se fuder' is more common in everyday speech.

definition: Literally 'go take it in the ass'; an extremely common dismissal expletive with anal sex imagery, roughly equivalent to 'go fuck yourself' but specifically evoking anal penetration of the target.
notes: Among the most frequently heard strong curses in Brazilian Portuguese; the anal sex framing implies the target is submissive or weak; often shortened in speech to 'tomar no cu' or even just 'no cu'; the concept maps imperfectly to any single English phrase because the anal framing is load-bearing in ways that 'go fuck yourself' is not.

definition: Colloquial spelling and pronunciation variant of 'vá se foder'; 'go fuck yourself'; uses the indicative 'vai' and the variant spelling 'fuder,' reflecting everyday spoken Brazilian Portuguese.
notes: Functionally identical to 'vá se foder'; the 'vai' indicative form is more colloquial and dominant in informal speech and writing; 'fuder' vs 'foder' reflects a common vowel reduction in fast speech; the two forms are interchangeable in all registers.

definition: Literally 'wooden ass'; an insult for a stingy, ungenerous, or obstinately unyielding person, whose orifice is metaphorically too rigid to give anything.
notes: The 'wood' metaphor implies an anus so tight as to be impenetrable — hence miserly or unyielding; primarily means cheap or stubbornly obstinate rather than being a simple anatomical insult; 'cu' (ass/anus) is also used as a standalone insult or exclamation, but 'cu de pau' is a fixed idiomatic compound with its own distinct meaning.
